rows.stem:
There are four solutions A, B, C, and D with pH values as follows :

| Solution | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pH | 2.0 | 7.0 | 8.0 | 12.0 |

Which solution(s) would liberate hydrogen gas with zinc ?
rows.solution:
Zinc gives hydrogen gas with an acid and also with a strong base. Solution A (pH 2.0) is strongly acidic and solution D (pH 12.0) is strongly basic, so both liberate hydrogen with zinc:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2}\)

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\) (sodium zincate)

Solution B (pH 7.0) is neutral and solution C (pH 8.0) is only weakly basic, so neither gives hydrogen with zinc.

This is option (C) A and D.

rows.stem: In torch lights and head lights of vehicles, the bulb is placed

options.label: A
options.text: between the pole and the focus of the reflector.

options.label: B
options.text: very near to the focus of the reflector.

options.label: C
options.text: between the focus and centre of curvature of the reflector.

options.label: D
options.text: at the centre of curvature of the reflector.

rows.solution:
Rays from a source placed at the principal focus of a concave mirror become parallel to the principal axis after reflection. So the bulb in a torch or a vehicle's headlight is placed very near the focus of its concave reflector, which sends out a strong, parallel beam of light.

This is option (B) very near to the focus of the reflector.

rows.stem:
Choose the option giving correct matching the items given in Column – I & II.

| Column – I | Column – II |
|---|---|
| A. Physical environment | (i) Ozone layer depletion |
| B. Exposure to UV radiation | (ii) Bacteria and Fungi |
| C. Chlorofluoro Carbon compounds | (iii) Abiotic components |
| D. Decomposers | (iv) Skin Cancer |
rows.solution:
The physical environment is the abiotic component of an ecosystem: A matches (iii). Exposure to UV radiation can cause skin cancer: B matches (iv). Chlorofluorocarbons deplete the ozone layer: C matches (i). Bacteria and fungi are decomposers: D matches (ii).

This is option (B) A: (iii); B: (iv); C: (i); D: (ii).

rows.stem: The thread like structures that develop on a moist slice of bread in Rhizopus are
rows.solution:
On a moist slice of bread, Rhizopus (bread mould) grows as a network of fine thread-like structures called hyphae. The tiny blob-on-a-stick structures that develop on them are the sporangia, which carry the spores.

This is option (D) Hyphae.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The change in the focal length of an eye lens in human beings is caused by the action of
rows.solution:
The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens. When they relax the lens becomes thin and its focal length increases (for distant objects); when they contract the lens becomes thick and its focal length decreases (for nearby objects). This is the power of accommodation.

This is option (B) ciliary muscles.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Testes in human males are located outside the abdominal cavity in scrotum.

**Reason (R) :** Scrotum provides a lower temperature than the normal body temperature for sperm formation.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The testes in human males lie outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum, so the Assertion is true.

Sperm formation needs a temperature lower than the normal body temperature, and the scrotum provides this. So the Reason is true and explains why the testes are located there.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
How is an electric impulse created in human nervous system ? Identify the parts of a neuron which helps the nerve impulse to travel

(i) towards the cell body

(ii) away from the cell body
rows.solution:
Information acquired at the end of the dendritic tip of a nerve cell (neuron) sets off a chemical reaction, and this reaction creates an electrical impulse. The impulse then travels along the neuron.

(i) The impulse travels towards the cell body through the dendrites.

(ii) It travels away from the cell body through the axon.

rows.stem: With the help of an example, explain how does the feedback mechanism regulate the hormone secretion.
rows.solution:
The timing and amount of hormone released are regulated by feedback mechanisms: the level of the substance the hormone controls is itself the signal that raises or lowers its secretion.

Example: insulin, from the pancreas, controls the blood sugar level. When the sugar level in the blood rises, the pancreas detects it and produces more insulin. As the blood sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw magnetic field lines produced around a straight current carrying conductor passing through a cardboard. How will the strength of the magnetic field change when the point where magnetic field is to be determined is moved away from the conductor ?
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw a horizontal cardboard sheet with a straight conductor passing vertically through its centre, connected in a circuit with a battery and a key (an ammeter and a rheostat may also be shown). Around the conductor, on the cardboard, draw a set of concentric circles centred on the wire: these are the magnetic field lines. Mark the direction of the current in the wire and the direction of the field lines on the circles, which by the right-hand thumb rule is anticlockwise (seen from above) for a current flowing upwards.

The strength of the magnetic field decreases as the point is moved away from the conductor: the field is inversely proportional to the distance from the wire, so the circles also lie farther apart at larger distances.

rows.stem:
(i) What property do acids and bases have in common ? Explain it with an example.

(ii) A compound which is prepared from gypsum has the property of hardening when mixed with water.

Identify the compound and write its formula. How is this compound prepared ? Describe it in the form of a chemical equation only.
rows.solution:
(i) Both acids and bases produce ions when added to water: acids give hydrogen ions (\(\mathrm{H^+}\), present as \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) and bases give hydroxide ions (\(\mathrm{OH^-}\)). That is also why solutions of both conduct electricity.

\(\mathrm{HCl + H_2O \rightarrow H_3O^+ + Cl^-}\)

\(\mathrm{NaOH \xrightarrow{H_2O} Na^+ + OH^-}\)

(ii) The compound is Plaster of Paris, calcium sulphate hemihydrate, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_2O}\).

It is prepared by heating gypsum at 373 K:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O \xrightarrow{373\ K} CaSO_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Write the chemical name and Molecular formula of tooth enamel.

(ii) How does it get corroded ? What is the preventive measure for this ?
rows.solution:
(i) Tooth enamel is calcium hydroxyapatite (a form of calcium phosphate), \(\mathrm{Ca_{10}(PO_4)_6(OH)_2}\), also written \(\mathrm{Ca_5(PO_4)_3(OH)}\). It is the hardest substance in the body. (The marking scheme prints \(\mathrm{Ca_3(PO_4)_2}\), which is the formula of plain calcium phosphate, not of hydroxyapatite.)

(ii) Bacteria present in the mouth break down the sugar and food particles left after eating and produce acids. When the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5, the acid starts to corrode the enamel and tooth decay begins.

Prevention: clean the mouth after eating and brush the teeth with toothpaste. Toothpastes are generally basic, so they neutralise the excess acid.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
A person is unable to see clearly a poster fixed on a distant wall. He however sees it clearly when standing at a distance of about 2 m from the wall.

(a) Draw ray diagram to show the formation of image by his eye lens when he is far away from the wall.

(b) List two possible reasons of this defect of vision.

(c) Draw ray diagram to show the correction of this defect using appropriate lens.
rows.solution:
The person can see nearby objects clearly but not distant ones, so he suffers from myopia (near-sightedness).

(a) Ray diagram: draw the eye with parallel rays coming from the distant poster (object at infinity). After passing through the eye lens the rays meet at a point in front of the retina, not on it, so the image on the retina is blurred. Mark the arrows on the rays.

(b) Two possible reasons: (i) excessive curvature of the eye lens; (ii) elongation of the eyeball.

(c) Ray diagram: place a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power in front of the eye. The parallel rays from the distant object first diverge through the lens, as if they came from the far point of the myopic eye (here about 2 m away), and the eye lens then brings them to a focus on the retina. Mark the arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
State the change in colour observed in each of the following cases mentioning the reason :

(a) Silver chloride is exposed to sunlight.

(b) A piece of zinc is dipped in ferrous sulphate solution.

(c) Copper powder is strongly heated in air.
rows.solution:
(a) White silver chloride turns grey in sunlight, because it decomposes into silver (grey) and chlorine:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag + Cl_2}\)

(b) The pale green colour of the ferrous sulphate solution fades and the solution becomes colourless. Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron and colourless zinc sulphate is formed:

\(\mathrm{Zn + FeSO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + Fe}\)

(c) Brown copper powder turns black, because it is oxidised to black copper(II) oxide:

\(\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Name the two types of pollination and differentiate between them.

(b) Explain the post fertilization changes that occur in the ovary of a flower.

(c) Given below is a diagram of a germinating seed. Label the parts that

(i) gives rise to future shoot.

(ii) gives rise to future root system.

(iii) stores food.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a small boxed drawing of a germinating seed (two rounded lobes with the embryo axis between them) with three parts marked by leader lines to the letters A, B and C; which part each letter marks is the quantity under test in part (c) and is withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(a) The two types of pollination are self-pollination and cross-pollination.

| Self-pollination | Cross-pollination |
|---|---|
| Transfer of pollen grains from the stamen to the stigma of the same flower, or of another flower on the same plant | Transfer of pollen grains from a flower of one plant to a flower of a different plant (of the same kind) |

(b) Any three:

1. The zygote divides several times to form an embryo within the ovule.

2. The ovule develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into a seed.

3. The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit.

4. The sepals, petals, stamens, style and stigma shrivel and fall off.

(c) (i) A, the plumule, gives rise to the future shoot.

(ii) B, the radicle, gives rise to the future root system.

(iii) C, the cotyledon, stores food.
